newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia reassures investors over ownership issue.
newsitem.headline: Croatia reassures investors over ownership issue.

text.p: Croatian Privatisation Minister Ivan Penic reassured investors on Friday that shares bought on the secondary market from a fraudulent source would not be challenged by the government.
"Investors who purchased shares bona fide on the secondary market are completely safe," Penic told a press conference..
"The Croatian government guarantees the safety of all such contracts.".

The Privatisation Fund recently announced that some 9,000 people were found to have exceeded the legal limit for purchase of shares at discount under the employees buyout scheme, which was set at 20,000 German marks ($12,500) per person.
Croatia's National Security Council consequently called for all such illegal contracts, worth some 300 million marks ($200 million) in total, to be annulled.
The decision of the influential political body sent shock waves through the fragile Croatian capital market, although it was not immediately clear what sort of concrete legal steps would be taken.
Trading almost came to a halt last week, but showed signs of recovery towards the end of this week as it became increasingly clear that the Fund would deal with the issue with extreme care.

Penic said the Fund would annul contracts for people who bought shares at a discount at several different firms and exceeded the limit, but would not challenge those who bought from them on the secondary market. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
